basis: Cerebral cortical malformation and cerebellar hypoplasia define this neurologic disorder.
Microphthalmia, lung hypoplasia and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; cardiac malformations occur in 30-79%. Renal and gastrointestinal defects are generally occasional.
Generalized dystonia, cerebellar atrophy and cognitive deterioration; laryngeal and ocular movement abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Peroxisomal disorder with defining brain and liver disease; retinal degeneration affects 80-99%. Cap excludes skeletal abnormalities (80-99%) and hearing loss (30-79%).
Clonal mast-cell neoplasm; hepatic infiltration/hepatomegaly, intestinal malabsorption and osteoporosis each occur in 30-79%. Skin lesions and liver dysfunction are less frequent.
Primary penile carcinoma affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; HPV association does not make the carcinoma an infection.
Neurodevelopmental impairment is typical across substantial chromosome 10 duplications; unspecified duplicated interval prevents reliable additional organ assignments.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; white-matter disease and developmental impairment in 7/7, visual impairment with optic disc pallor in 5/7. Weakness can reflect neurologic disease.
Neoplasm originates in the prostate, a reproductive organ outside the axes; urinary tract damage is not established across this umbrella.
Nonsyndromic inherited hearing loss; hearing impairment reported in 4/4 patients.
Childhood epilepsy with developmental impairment or epileptic encephalopathy directly affects brain function.
Substance-use disorder has no axis; overdose injury and injection-associated infections are separate conditions.
Record identifies an inherited platelet enzyme-activity phenotype; platelet biology maps to haematologic, but a clinical disease definition is absent.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; congenital contractures occur in 13/30 patients (~43%), establishing common structural musculoskeletal involvement.
Profound encephalopathy and movement disorder; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic. Feeding difficulty and hypotonia do not establish separate organ damage.
Developmental delay and skeletal malformations characterize the syndrome; clinodactyly occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac defects are occasional; pigment spots do not establish skin damage.
Central and peripheral demyelination with autonomic dysfunction; bladder symptoms, constipation and orthostatic hypotension do not establish direct urinary, gut or vascular damage.
Functional impairment of gallbladder emptying or biliary sphincter function; gallbladder and bile ducts belong to hepatic.
Definition and anatomical location specify a neoplasm of jaw bone; oral-system ancestry alone does not establish gastrointestinal involvement.
Thoracic skeletal dysplasia with defining pulmonary hypoplasia/respiratory failure; ventricular septal defect reported in 1/2 patients. Cardiac frequency rests on a very small cohort.
Traumatic injury of the upper brachial plexus causes arm paralysis; weakness reflects nerve injury rather than primary muscle disease.
Defining microphthalmia, pulmonary hypoplasia (4/5) and severe neurodevelopmental impairment; intestinal malrotation in 2/7 (~29%) is below threshold.
Mycobacterial infection of male reproductive organs; renal or pulmonary disease is not established by this genital-site concept.
Inherited cardiac channelopathy causing shortened repolarization and potentially lethal atrial or ventricular arrhythmias.
Inherited coagulation factor XI deficiency; mucosal bleeding does not establish direct organ damage, and joint or gastrointestinal hemorrhage occurs in only 1-4%.
